# Exploratory Data Analysis — Kforce Data Analyst project

All data is **synthetic** (generated by `R/01_data_generation.R`,
`set.seed(42)`). Five service channels, 730 days (2024-01-01 to
2025-12-30), plus a daily pipeline-health log with 25 injected
data-quality incidents.

```{r load}
kpi <- read.csv("../data/synthetic/kpi_daily.csv")
kpi$date <- as.Date(kpi$date)
health <- read.csv("../data/synthetic/pipeline_health_daily.csv")
health$date <- as.Date(health$date)
str(kpi)
summary(kpi[, c("tickets_received", "sla_attainment_pct",
                "avg_handle_time_min", "csat_score")])
```

## Volume by channel

```{r volume}
aggregate(tickets_received ~ channel, data = kpi, FUN = mean)
```

## SLA attainment by channel

```{r sla}
aggregate(sla_attainment_pct ~ channel, data = kpi, FUN = mean)
```

## Weekly seasonality — the midweek peak

```{r weekly}
kpi$dow <- weekdays(kpi$date)
aggregate(tickets_received ~ dow, data = kpi, FUN = mean)
```

## Pipeline health — incident rate

```{r health}
table(health$is_anomaly, health$anomaly_type)
summary(health[, c("missing_rate_pct", "duplicate_rate_pct",
                   "late_feed_minutes", "null_rate_pct")])
```

## What the EDA says

1. Demand is strongly weekly-seasonal: midweek peaks, weekend
   troughs — any forecaster that ignores the 7-day cycle will fail.
2. SLA attainment varies by channel (Publishing Ops and Field
   Service run lowest) — the benchmark in Problem 3 is real.
3. Pipeline incidents are rare (~3.4% of days) but extreme when
   they happen — a threshold detector, not a classifier, is the
   right tool.
